utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We still have to deal with exhibits that were tendered previous days. Madam Registrar, could you please guide us through the documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D348/12B, videotape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution does object to the videotape on the basis of relevance. I think an objection was taken at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we will then further consider that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D1772, under seal, pseudonym sheet; D1773, map; D1774, map; D1776, map; D1775, map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Since there are no objections against these documents, they are admitted in the evidence and the Chamber has also decided that in respect of the videotape mentioned, Madam Registrar, is it correct that it is a D348/12B, that is at least what the --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is what the transcript says. The Chamber denies the objection and admits the videotape in evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: There is also outstanding Exhibit P3753 black and white photographs, set of five.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The objection the Defence has raised against the use of these photographs is denied. The photographs of the church, different photographs, are admitted into evidence. And where the Defence has objected also on the basis that it was exculpatory material that was not timely disclosed by the Prosecution, the Chamber considers that the Prosecution at the time they retrieved these photographs, it was not apparent to the Prosecution, at least, Prosecution told the Chamber that it was not apparent to them that this was exculpatory material, and the Chamber accepts that the Prosecution should not have considered it, should not have qualified it at that moment as exculpatory material. Where the Defence has explained that questions put to witnesses could have resulted in exculpatory evidence, that as such does not qualify the document as such as exculpatory. If the Prosecution takes its obligation seriously, that it has to disclose exculpatory material, it should become apparent in one way or another from that material itself that it would be exculpatory for the Defence. Having dealt with the documents, is the Defence ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are only halfway through our documents because we have yesterday's documents. Yes. Yes. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have conveyed to Madam Registrar rather late that I would like to address your Chamber for a few minutes. Do I have your permission to do so?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are several points that we need to address. Yesterday, we were able to note a high degree of nervousness. Yesterday, the Defence was exposed to two types of strange interventions. We were accused of making noise which we were not doing. We were reproached for a nonprofessional attitude, and at the end of the hearing, two representatives of the Prosecution stood up saying that the witness had greeted General Galic, and that this should be entered into the record. I should like to challenge anyone to assert that this witness greeted General Galic and not members of the Defence. And if anyone wishes to respond, I would like to have the proof of that on the spot. Secondly, supposing that this witness who experienced atrocities and who was victim of grave violations of humanitarian law and who was a young soldier under the orders of the general, supposing he did greet him, what is astonishing about that? Third point, there were Prosecution witnesses, and I am speaking by memory, I am speaking of Dr. Nakas, who upon leaving this auditorium greeted in a military way General Galic which is out of courtesy, and I didn't notice the Prosecution saying anything. Thirdly, witnesses of the Prosecution after testifying had wanted contact with me, the Prosecution gave them my telephone number, and I see nothing wrong with that. Also, the Defence did not make any gesture that would justify the accusation that behaviour was not professional. Now we come to a more technical matters. The question of lines. The Prosecution said that everything appearing in the transcript regarding the lines drawn by this witness should be redacted because they say it is not normal for a witness to draw lines. I remind you that all the maps given by the Prosecution carry lines mentioning angles or trajectories. If the Defence does not have the right when an already drawn maps are given to it, is not allowed to have its witnesses draw lines there seems to be a disequilibrium between the parties which is not understandable regardless of jurisdictions. A third point, Your Honour, the question of time. For this witness, I tried very quickly to put questions to this witness to such a degree that I was asked to slow down. In spite of that, a lot of time was lost and that was certainly not the fault of the Defence and it would be necessary that the time used by the Prosecution should be within the given limits and not beyond that. The system of the banking system, as I said the other day, was not accepted and it is not normal for the Prosecution to take so much time. Also, there was a decision rendered regarding a meeting of the 30th of October. We told you that we responded that very day, on the 30th of October. And this decision has to do with the need of dividing up the exhibits according to witnesses. I should like to recall that the Prosecution did not do so in its own case. It only did it from one week to another, on a weekly basis, in other words, and we understood your decision to mean that the Defence should do so for its whole case. Clearly, if that were to be the case there would be inequality of treatment and we don't know whether your decision was confirmed after reading our letter of the 30th of October or whether it needs further specification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What exactly -- it is not in my recollection that we took a decision, as a matter of fact. You brought to our attention that you replied to the complaint in writing, and I don't -- it is not in my recollection that we have taken a decision. So before you ask us to review a decision or to reconsider the matter, what was our decision and where do we find it exactly? I might make a mistake, but, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I cannot verify right now, but I think that you indicated the following: Prosecution is right when it was presenting its interpretation of mail. The Prosecution is right, et cetera, and if you tell us that the Prosecution is right in its interpretation of the -- your decision, this is perhaps not a decision but almost a decision and that is how we understood it. I shall try to find your exact words and quote from them later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You wanted us to reconsider the matter. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it is a decision, yes, if there is no decision, everything is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have to consider the matter. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to the last point, Mr. President, when you said that the other day, Mr. Piletta-Zanin interrupted and said that he had replied and that he wanted you to read his reply before you made the decision and that's where it was left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that is what we then it tended to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to the other matters, the many matters raised by Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I don't propose to reply to all of them. When we objected yesterday to noise coming from the Defence side, specifically what we meant is that quite audibly from here we could make out conversations, although we could not understand them, between Defence counsel in the Serbian language and it concerned us greatly, that if we could hear it, then certainly the witness, and we thought it, and continue to think it, inappropriate. Although we only made that observation once, it is something which we hear repeatedly. Mr. President, two further matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just already address this matter. I observed yesterday that when conversations between General Galic and Defence counsel started at a relatively high volume, that they seemed to become aware of this and the volume then was put down. I observed that and I appreciate that the Defence is aware that no conversation should be held in a language the Chamber cannot follow in the presence of a witness. So I do understand. I do agree with you that it should be avoided. I also observed that at least yesterday that where it started the wrong way it continued the right way. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, two other matters. Firstly, I would be grateful if we could, as a matter of course, have an update each Friday from the Defence as to the order of witnesses to be called the following week. And more particularly, that any update be a running list. In other words, rather than have a list of witnesses for two weeks time, every time we get a list of witnesses, it be from the next witness onwards. Secondly, Mr. President, an issue that I have raised a number of times is evidence being elicited from Defence witnesses which is contrary to Prosecution evidence and which has not been put to any of the relevant Prosecution witnesses. That also is a concern because the -- some of that evidence has not been the subject of notice to us. Mr. President, it seems to me that the appropriate course for the Prosecution to take is to object to that evidence being elicited on those grounds. I am in your hands as to the way we should do that. The possibilities are that each time it happens, and we have had an opportunity to do a double-check, that we formally object and ask that the evidence be redacted because, of course, it is given without notice. Mr. President, it would also be appropriate, I think, if we were to assist you with a motion, in other words, a submission in writing on that issue. Normally, that would be done in response to an adverse decision against the Prosecution which would seem to necessitate us as a matter of logic in taking those various objections. I appreciate the time constraints and I wonder whether in view of the time pressures and in view of the many submissions I have made to this effect in the past, it could be taken as sufficient -- a sufficient foundation for the written submission and I could simply, in the course of next week, file that seeking a response that such evidence from here on should be rejected. The Trial Chamber could then consider its position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it be a practical solution that the Prosecution sets out in writing in general terms the complaints it has about the way the Defence is proceeding in this respect, that the Defence would respond to that, and that at a suitable occasion whether the Prosecution finds a moment where it would like to object against the way the Defence is proceeding, that it objects or asks for redaction, and then refers at that moment to the written exchange, views, so that we then can take a decision, but that we have prepared that in writing, at least the parties have prepared the arguments for such situations in writing and that we then wait until the first time that we are facing this problem. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am not going to respond in substance. The Defence is working until very late at night. It has a very small team. When we begin to prove things now, we are asking for the transcript to be redacted now, why, because we are prove the opposite from the Prosecution, nothing else. I wish to underline that on the 29th of October, 2002, the Defence clearly indicated to the Prosecution everything that the witness could be saying. All this is very precise. There is no ambush there. And I do not understand when witnesses come to testify and say something, act in the same way as all other witnesses have done, we are told, stop, "they are Defence witnesses and passages need to be redacted," obviously those that prove the case of the Defence. This in our view is evidence of total disrespect of the truth. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I just indicate that the procedural outline that you have given is acceptable to the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would the Defence be willing to respond then to such a submission so that the Chamber can decide whenever the situation occurs?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we absolutely do not have time, and we are reproached for speaking Serbian. I am reproached for this. I am reproached for speaking French. And when I have meetings in English, I am reproached for speaking in English. We are criticised for so many things as the Defence. We simply don't have the physical time to engage in this effort. This is a strategy of harassment and exhaustion of the Defence. If it is felt that General Galic should not have Defence counsel able to do its work, we should be told straight away, "we are going to exhaust you and you can't do anything." If that is what is wanted, let us be told that. I would like to know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please explain what you meant by you saying "that you are going to exhaust us, and that we can't do anything," Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I will be glad to. At present we are engaging in some very delicate preparations for the Defence case. I have to interrogate each of the witnesses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I asked you what you meant when you said: "We are going to exhaust you, and you can't do anything." I would like you to just explain these words. That is what appears in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I will be glad to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What I especially would like to know since I was listening to the English channel, when you said in French that this is going to exhaust you, or that you were going to exhaust us? That's, as a matter of fact, the clarification I would like to have in order to avoid whatever misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't know whether I am going to exhaust you, but I never said that I would exhaust you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the only clarification that I would line to have, because it is then wrongly written in the transcript. I will take care always to switch to French when you speak. I do understand that the answer of the Defence is that they do not agree with the proposed procedural approach. Since the parties disagree, the Chamber will decide what the procedural way we are dealing with this matter will be. Having said this, I think the Defence could call its next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just before that happens, there is still a matter of a running list. And I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the running list. The last list that has been provided by the Defence was that -- what is the last list, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, so that we --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Ms. Pilipovic will address you because we had to divide up our tasks as you know, and she is fully au courant with the matter. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the last list the one attached to the letter of the 29th of October?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This starts with a name which --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A female name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, a female name.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, except that today the Defence will submit a list, the list for next week. The schedule is more or less the same except that we were informed last night that one witness for certain reasons will not be able to come here next week. So today after the session, I will submit the list. There won't be many changes. More or less there will be the same witness, except for one, the number three on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Will that list start with the witness examined today or, I mean, is there a gap between the witnesses that are examined now and that are still going to testify, and the first one on the list? What the Prosecution is asking you is to provide lists where the first name is also the next witness you will call, and that could avoid any confusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the list for next week will begin with the witness who starts today, unless he is finished today. So it will start with this witness and then we will have the continuation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then we have the -- I think, Mr. Ierace, that is what you --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you,

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- What you are seeking. Then we can start -- we will consider the matter of the documents whether they have to be related to a specific witness or not, where in writing the Defence responded that they could not relate the documents to specific witnesses. We will consider the matter and we will give you a ruling on that. Ms. Pilipovic, are you ready to call your next witness? And Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, do we still -- because the Chamber is not informed -- do we have to take any decision in respect of protective measures or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I even hear that you can even understand me in the language I use. Before giving testimony in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require that you make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text of this declaration we be now given to you by the usher. Will you please make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. You will first be examined by counsel for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, good morning?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please introduce yourself, surname and date of birth. My name is Izo Golic, father's name Velija [Realtime transcript read in error "Delija"]. I was born on the 5th of January 1954 [as interpreted], village of Zakum, municipality of Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us what is your profession?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I am a transport engineer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us in 1992, and we are only speaking about the period from 1992 through 1994 where did you live and where did you work?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I lived in the place where I was born in Zakum, near Rogatica and all the time I worked in Rogatica. For a while in the state company Tehnotrans from Rogatica which was a transport company and later on --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Witness. I would just like to ask you to speak a little more slowly considering that the interpreters have to translate what you say. And since we are speaking the same language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before my colleague proceeds with the question, could the date of birth of this witness be clarified because what I see on the transcript is not entirely consistent with what we have and it does affect the manner in which we proceed with searches in respect of this witness. So it would be very helpful if the date of birth would be clarified and the father's name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there seems to be confusion. The witness has answered that question, but do I understand that you have received information that is different from the testimony of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: From what I see on the transcript. From what we have received from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, could you tell us, when were you born?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 5th of January, 1959, in the village of Zakum near Rogatica and I studied in Sarajevo, if that means anything to anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Father's name?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Velija. Velija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Golic, you told us that in 1992, you lived and worked in Rogatica. Could you tell us, did you serve military service and where?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I served in the former JNA like all the citizens of the former Yugoslavia. After I completed my faculty in 1984, I served the military service in Subotica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us or what is your military specialty?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I was 11206. I was a server, crew member of the -- later on commander --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat part of the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the latter part of the answer. You said "I was a server crew member of," and then could you please repeat that part of your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I served in the JNA in Subotica in 1984. And my military specialty was 11206. I was a server and, later on, commander of the platoon of the mortar, 120 millimetre, M-74, M-75.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, you are using the word "11206." That does not mean anything to me at this very moment. Could you tell us what that is, what that number stands for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Rules of service in the former Yugoslavia provided certain abilities, certain military specialties, abilities, and this is just a code of the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, in September 1992, could you tell us where were you?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: In September 1992, I was on the Sarajevo front and my unit was in the area of the village of Petrovici below Mount Trebevic on the south-west side near Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, I would just like you to answer the questions as slowly and briefly, please. Mr. Golic, when you told us where you were in 1992, could you tell us what military unit did you belong to?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I was a member of a mortar battery, 120 millimetre within the Rogatica Battalion as part of the 1st Romanija Brigade of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you tell us that you were a member of the Rogatica Battalion in 1992, could you tell us when was Rogatica Battalion established?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: The Rogatica Battalion was established in 1992 in March, following the breakup of the units of the former JNA in that area because of the desertion of the units by members of Muslim members of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Golic, you told us that the Rogatica Battalion was established in March 1992. Could you tell us what was the duty, what was the task of this battalion?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: If I can clarify. So it was established after the first demonstration, that is the first barricades [Realtime transcript read in error "barracks"] were set up in Sarajevo after the killing of the member of a wedding party in Sarajevo --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that there is a problem in the English transcript. I can read "first barracks." I am not sure that is what is correct. What I believe that the transcript -- I cannot repeat it, but I will have to -- I have to state it here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you clarified your answer, you say: "So it was established after the first demonstration that is the first, what? I see that you are reading the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After the first barricades in Sarajevo, that is after the 1st of March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear. Would you please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, did you personally receive call-up papers to join this unit?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: No. I simply found out on the 3rd of March that all Serb population was going of their own self initiative in the village of Gucevo near Rogatica and this arrival was not something that I was informed of. This was something spontaneous of the Serb population from this region where I lived, where I lived and worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Golic, when you told us that in September 1992, as a member of Rogatica Battalion, you were on the positions as you told us in the village of Petrovici below -- sorry Mount Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Mount Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mount Trebevic. Could you tell us that when was it that as a member of the Rogatica Battalion you arrived on the positions that were the positions of the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: We arrived there on the 3rd of May after the events with respect to the barracks and the departure of the former JNA from Sarajevo, and the events in the Dobrovoljacka Street. It was on the 3rd of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Golic, as a member of the Rogatica Battalion, could you tell us how strong was the Rogatica Battalion?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: To start with, there were 450 people, but because of some personal fear or other reasons, they didn't go to Sarajevo, so only 250 of us went to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you tell us left for Sarajevo, could you tell us who called you to go to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: As a battalion, we were called and gathered in Gucevo on the 4th of April following the Muslim Ramadan holiday, and when they were celebrating and firing from our weapons in our regions too and these barricades were set up, also in Sarajevo and we were called together as a battalion in Gucevo. So this was a mobilisation of the battalion on the 4th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the month of May when you arrived in Sarajevo, could you tell us to which positions did your battalion come?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: We came to the positions where the Serb population had established and set up its barricades. So the infantry units were had their positions and the positions from the Jewish cemetery until the bridge, that is, towards the Executive Council. That is the bridge on the -- Vrbanja bridge and then from the southern part of Miljacka River, near the Brotherhood and Unity Bridge and the Grbavica stadium, and then along Vraca, alongside Vraca until the beginning up there towards Mojmilo hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Can I just clarify something. The mortar battery had the position on old field in Lukavica of the football club, Lukavica. During the following night, we had to withdraw to the village of Ivanici because we were under intense sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Golic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation], Mr. President, apparently what doesn't appear in the transcript is Ivanici.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is the village on the other side of the hill --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Golic. Mr. Golic, could you tell us for the transcript, you withdrew from Lukavica to the village --

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: From the field of the Lukavica football club some 500 metres we draw to the other side of the hill and the village is Ivanici. Ivanici, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Golic, could you tell us the Rogatica Battalion, you say this is a battery, a mortar battery. Could you tell us were there companies within the battalion?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: There were two infantry companies and one mortar battalion of the Rogatica Battalion. And I said that infantry companies had their positions from the Jewish cemetery through the Vrbanja bridge and the Zeljin stadium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are telling us that you were in a mortar battery. Can you tell us how many weapons did your mortar battery have?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. The artillery, we had six pieces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people were there in the battery?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: It wasn't up to establishment strength because many people left and it was composed of people who -- that was not their military specialty and there were only 45 people and in establishment strength should have been 65.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the command of your battalion, where was it located?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: The command of the battalion was located, to start with, in Vraca, in a building near the monument. And at this time, that is from August, it was in at the guesthouse by Trebevic near the tennis courts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, your mortar battery, did it have its command post?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: The commander was with the battery except that when he had to be at reconnaissance position, that is on the observation position where he was able to tell us where to fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us these two companies that were part of the battalion, where did they have their command post?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, these two companies, where did they have their command post?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Immediately after -- behind the demarcation line, the command of the first company was by the Catholic nun's home and the second one was in a coffee bar somewhere towards the Zagrebacka Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, now you've described the composition of the units you belonged to and the weapons that your battery had, could you tell us, did you, as a member of the mortar battery, did you receive targets for your battery?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. At that time I was a commander of the second firing platoon and we were -- we received the targets from the superior command and most of the time this was done verbally and occasionally the chief of artillery would come personally, the chief of the artillery of the brigade, Mr. Grajic and these targets were mostly those from which firing was opened -- fire was opened by Muslim forces on our targets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since I was listening instead of looking, there was a written message from our transcribers please to slow down for the record. As you know the transcribers express themselves with writing, rather than Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. speaking. Could you please, not only for the interpreters, but also for those who have to transcribe whatever is said in this courtroom, slow down a bit. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, you told us that you received targets for your battery. Could you tell us, you personally, did you know which targets they were?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Considering that I was practically in the battery the only one who really had the military specialty, the relevant military specialty, the battery commander was a late Mr. Orasanin and his deputy was Milorad Karicki from Rogatica and --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have asked you something else.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I have to tell you that I was asked and I always knew these targets considering because that was what I was qualified for.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, one part of what the answer -- what the witness said has not been translated, which is not in the transcript. I don't think that something that is very important -- that is essential. I am just saying this for the booth. Thank you. I don't think it is essential.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. A part of an answer has not been transcribed when you, Ms. Pilipovic, subsequently asked the witness to answer to the question or is there another. Could you please indicate page what and what lines?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was just before, but it isn't very important, Mr. President. I will check if it is necessary by listening to the tape. I don't think that it changes the meaning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was asking what part, what page what line you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was around line 10 on page 21, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic, you asked then the witness to give a response to your question rather than what he said at that moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, so you told us that considering your specialty and your qualifications, you were the person qualified to work on mortars. Now, I asked you whether you had a targeting schedule?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us in 1992, what targets were the ones targeted by your battery? And I am talking about targets on the other side.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Here, I just have to stress that before we arrived in the village of Petrovici, we were in the village of Ivanici. We had completely different targets than the ones we had in Petrovici. So do you want me to tell you about the targets we had in Ivanici?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us when you arrived in the village of Ivanici what were the targets you had?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Our targets were the ones that the Muslim forces opened fire on us on the members of our battalion located in Grbavica. So these targets went from Zetra to the part of the Rudjer Boskovic Street through Kosevo tunnel, and then the roundabout way for the Olympic Games, and then above Velisici above Rudjer Boskovic Street two mortars were located, two mortars of the Muslim army, and then following that line, along the demarcation line on Grbavica, and then Brotherhood and Unity Bridge where Muslims often tried to break through onto our territory --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: To slow down. We have to get a good record of what the witness is saying. And I think I should put on the record that what we are having now is something which we have not been apprised of. We have received three summaries of what this witness was to come to testify about from the Defence. We have asked for further and better particulars. And we were not advised that this witness was going to speak about mortar targets or from where there were mortar positions within the confrontation lines. Much of this we were not aware of that the Defence were going to be eliciting this type of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I put that on the record. The witness is here. I suppose his evidence will have to be heard. I would just ask that it be clearly record what is said so that we can do whatever checks we can in the short time we have.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that if you disagree and if you say that you informed the Prosecution, I would like to see the summary -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, here is what you saw the other day. And I would like to read it. "For each of the witness, in a generic sense, each of the witness will testify on confusion between military and civilian targets, the number, the existence of protection means, et cetera." So it is clearly indicated that the witnesses will testify, all the military men, on the importance of military structures and their number and position obviously. This was clearly stated. And I even said, in a generic sense, all weapons, small arms fire, heavy weapons, et cetera. So this objection is simply intended to waste precious time whereas this formal indication was in the hands of Mr. Stamp and I saw it the other day, in the binder of Mr. Ierace, so this is a strategy that is being applied. A bellicose strategy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin is referring to the general observation, the general outline valid for --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I don't know if it is appropriate that we receive summaries of what a witness will speak of in a generic general global omnibus sentence. We have received summaries with specifics to which this witness is not testifying about. He is testifying about things which are not in the summaries, three summaries that we have received from the Defence in respect to this named witness. He is testifying to things which we have not received in the summaries, even after we are asked for further particulars in respect to this named witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You might have noticed that some issues, Mr. Stamp, are mentioned as being the subject of testimony of all the witnesses, and then further specification -- specifics are given in relation to each witness. Let's -- we will consider the matter. Let's now proceed as you suggested, but, Mr. Golic, may I ask you to slow down, at least so that we have clear information in the transcript on your testimony. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic --

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: May I just complete my previous answer, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wait a moment, please. You first told us that the first positions, or rather the targets that you had scheduled were in the area of Kosevo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us from which -- with which weapons and from which positions was Kosevo targeted by the opposing side?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: The opposing side in those days at the beginning had 120 millimetre mortars at those positions. It had two tanks and a mortar of 120 millimetres that was mounted on a lorry, maybe two, I am not sure, which would come out of the tunnel, open fire and go back into the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: And they also had two mortars mounted on a railway truck behind the station building of Sarajevo's railway -- new railway station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So you also said that they had two mortars near the railway station building. Can you tell us which one?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: The new Sarajevo railway station near the turning tracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, let us be quite specific. You are talking about these positions and distribution of artillery pieces of the BH Army, you are referring to positions that you had as targets from Ivanici or Petrovici?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Ivanici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you listed the targets in the area of Kosevo, can you tell us during which period of time was the BH Army acting or opening fire from these positions?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: This was the period from the beginning of our stationing in Ivanici until the end of July 1992. And their actions were on a continuous basis. And let me point out that we often registered the intervals between their fire and the artillery pieces used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, you told us that in September you were in Petrovici.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us in September 1992 which were your target schedules, the targets being from where the Muslim forces were acting?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: The maximum range was 6.300 metres. So our range couldn't go further than the Jewish cemetery, the deployment of the Muslim army below Zlatiste and very rarely did we open fire from August. Our battery didn't really operate because observers of SFOR had already arrived. They regularly visited our positions. They were familiar with everything so that our operations were much rarer and far between.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Golic, in September 1992, you were in Petrovici, that is your battery was there. Can you tell us until when you remained in that position?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: We remained in that position until mid-October, around the 20th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether in October 1992 you were given a different assignment. What happened to your battalion deployment?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: We received information from representatives of the Rogatica Brigade who came to seek assistance. Because after the 15th of October, there was a very powerful offensive by Muslim forces from the direction of Gorazde, against the Trnovo, Kosici et cetera, south of Rogatica and the danger threatened that the Turkish army [Realtime transcript read in error "turbish army"] could capture Rogatica. And we were withdrawn to our area, and let me also point out that with the arrival in Rogatica the battalion was disbanded and attached to the Rogatica Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just for clarification of the transcript. I see here "turbish army" and I'm not sure if that is what I heard the witness say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Turkish.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. That is how we called it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, did you say that in 1992, the Rogatica Battalion was disbanded?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: It was reassigned to the Rogatica Brigade with different assignments and it didn't exist as a separate battalion after we returned to Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more piece of information in connection with the Rogatica Brigade. Which corps did the Rogatica Brigade belong to? Do you personally know that?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. This was the light Rogatica Brigade. It was separate. I think we belonged to the Zvornik Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Golic, when you were telling us about the deployment of the artillery of the BH Army, do you know whether the BH Army had in its possession infantry weaponry and did it use those weapons against your battalion?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: In my opinion, no. I know that the Muslim forces were armed, if not better than us, than as well as we were with small arms and infantry weapons. It is true that they had somewhat fewer artillery pieces, but the situation changed when the barracks was -- the Marshal Tito Barracks was handed over in Sarajevo, and I personally felt this on my own skin because I was frequently exposed to their artillery fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, slow down, please. Mr. Golic, my question was whether you had knowledge as to whether the BH Army had in its possession infantry weapons and which kind of weapons?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. They had automatic rifles, as we did, Pam anti-aircraft machine-guns, M-70 machine-guns, M-84 machine-guns and they did not lag behind us in terms of the infantry weaponry. I personally was able to convince myself because I had a transaction in Sarajevo, that in the Skenderija Street on the 1st of April 1992 we entered an apartment as civilians. We were not members of the army at the time. We were looking for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I stop you at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is not only a matter of slowing down, but we are under certainly time constraints in this court. Would you please carefully listen to the question put to you by Ms. Pilipovic, answer that question, and if Ms. Pilipovic needs further information, she will certainly ask you for it. So the question was whether you had any knowledge as to the possession of infantry weapons and which kind of weapons. You started your answer by giving that information, but then you continued about a transaction on the 1st of April, an apartment, et cetera. If the source of your knowledge, if we need to know that, Ms. Pilipovic will surely ask you for it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I found an apartment full of infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand. Let me give you an example. If I would ask you whether you came to The Hague by car, and if you came by plane, just say "I did not come by car." And if Ms. Pilipovic would like to know what means of transportation you used, she will ask you, "if you did not come by car, how did you come." Yes. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, can you answer my question, please, on the basis of your personal knowledge, from which positions the BH Army acted with infantry weapons?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what those positions were?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Positions towards the Jewish cemetery on the eastern side of the Jewish cemetery where they frequently tried to break through our lines. Then positions on the north bank of the Miljacka river, towards Vraca, so from the assembly building, the Holiday Inn hotel, the Executive Council building, all the large buildings, the Hotel Bristol, the area around the Mechanical Engineering faculty towards the Brotherhood and Unity Bridge, around the barracks of the former JNA which they frequently sought to capture. So primarily around the Viktor Bubanj Barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Golic, in September 1992, so we are talking about the period between September and October, can you tell us whether there was combat in the area where you were?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: In the area of the battery, no, of course. But in the area of the battalion there was almost daily combat and attempts by the BH Army to capture our positions and to make breakthroughs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, when you listed the features, the buildings, which you say were the positions held by the BH Army, can you tell us in your opinion those buildings in relation to your positions, were they dominant or were your positions dominant? Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Up to the Miljacka river, they were on the same level. And around the Jewish cemetery, we were dominant and their positions above the tobacco factory and the other positions from which they fired with artillery weapons were dominant or on the same level. Their positions on Kosevo Hill, I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, at one point when you were listing these targets that you knew were the military positions of the BH Army, where their artillery and weapons were positioned, you also mentioned that they had mobile railway trucks?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us when you saw this and when the BH Army operated from those railway trucks, if at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am sorry. If might well be a matter of interpretation. Did we have evidence of mobile railway trucks?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we had something about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tracks, but trucks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mortars mounted on railway -- please find it Mr. -- Please proceed Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will assist you. I will try to find it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, could you please answer my question. When you say that they used railway trucks --

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: We had a 60 millimetre mortar within the infantry companion and there was some problems and I was invited to pull out the grenade from the mortar. This was in June. And I personally saw that mobile truck behind railway station, from the area of Vraca you can see it, behind the railway station building being moved. How it was moved we couldn't tell. Along the tracks it would be moved and then the 120-millimetre and 82-millimetre mortar fire was opened from it. So a shell -- they didn't have many shells. They would use two to four shells at a time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, page 25 line 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, I found it. Thanks very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a witness, Puhalo Savo, who was with me and saw this and who manned an 82 millimetre mortar.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, can you tell us, when you mentioned this railway station where you saw these trucks that were used to fire mortars from, 120- and 82-millimetre mortars, where was this station?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: It is close to the Velisici settlement. It is where the trains turn around. It is the end of the railway tracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you were looking at this from the Vraca positions?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, just below of our command post, east of our command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, can you tell us what distance that would be, that is the position of those trucks, and the position from where you were viewing them?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: As the crow flies, in my opinion, not more than 3 kilometres. I haven't looked at a map for a long time, so it wouldn't be more than three kilometres, in my judgment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, in view of the fact that you have indicated the spot from which the BH Army used mortars to open fire on you --

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: That was just one position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will come back to other positions. Tell us just how frequently they opened fire?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: They had some kind of a pattern, as if the artillery was given the task to open fire at given intervals. This was on a daily basis, but we knew roughly when they would open fire. And we sought to catch them when they were most sensitive, and in artillery the most sensitive moment for the opposing side is the moment when they open fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So you have just told us in answer to a question about the position of the mobile railway trucks. While you were on the lines held by your battery, did you have any personal knowledge or did you personally see the BH Army using any other vehicles as mobile positions?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. We had shifts in the battery. When a commander leaves, somebody has to stand in for him. So I personally went to the observation post and I saw a heavy-duty truck, I think it was a 13 ton truck that was coming out of a tunnel at the deviation of Kosevo, as it was called. It would fire and then quickly return to the tunnel. It was on a heavy-duty vehicle without the closed -- it was a Fap-13 truck. F-A-P 13 truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, can you tell us regarding this truck that you called a Fap-13. What weapon was mounted on it, if any?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. 120-millimetre launcher was mounted on it. Because we have observation means, binoculars, and so on, so that one could see this clearly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, in the region of Kosevo, you explained that the BH Army used a mobile mortar to fire from the tunnel. You also mentioned tanks.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I think they had two tanks, but I am not quite sure about that. They were stationed and dug in and you could only see the barrels. On the south-eastern slope of Hum towards Ciglana there is some earth dug up. It is an area that has not been built up. Just above the Rudjer Boskovic Street and to the right, above Velisici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Golic, did you personally see these tanks that you mentioned around the Kosevo tunnel, was fire opened from those tanks?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I personally did not see any fire coming from those tanks because I wasn't always on the observation post. But I did see them dug in and our scouts showed them to us so that those of us who were drawing in the targets could be as precise as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, you have explained to us or rather clarified the positions of your battalion. Can you tell us what the distance was between the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: From our position, the confrontation lines were between 3.000 and 5.300 metres. The azimuth was 53.00 to 7.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, if we look at the clock, could you find a suitable moment for a break.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This would be the most appropriate moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Ms. Pilipovic, the head of the section of interpretation services asked for copies of the witness summaries for the booth because very often we find names in there or other data which are of assistance for the interpreters -- and that is in most cases. Would you please provide an update, that even the most recent version, that always the interpreters are provided with the witness summaries.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Since we are on the issue of summaries, I wonder if I would address the court very briefly in the absence of the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could wait until the end of the testimony of this witness, or if would influence the course of the evidence then of course, we have to ask the witness to leave. If you would like to address the court in a more general way on the issue, I would rather do it after the witness has concluded his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I ask that it be done after his examination-in-chief because there are matters which I would ask the court to consider and perhaps to give some direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will then first continue the examination-in-chief and then you will have an opportunity -- please prepare it in such a way that we are spending just the time necessary, not more, and of course, not less. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my colleague will continue with further questions so that we can be more efficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. Examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you can, could you please answer with a yes or no if this is possible. Would you be able to do that?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, can you please tell us the elevated dominating positions that were held by the Muslim forces in Sarajevo to your knowledge, and at the time when you were in the Sarajevo area, very briefly, please?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: In the area of the Kosevo hill, around Zetra, towards the Kosevo stadium, and from our part of the front above the Jewish cemetery they were positioned towards the tower, and then on Mount Zlatiste when we arrived, we later on took Zlatiste and blocked it and they were also on the slopes of Mount Trebevic on Colina Kapa. So that means they were above our positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You gave us a list of these positions. Could you tell us the mountain in question --

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Can I just add something?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wait. Wait a minute. You will add later. But now one thing at a time, please. Could you please tell me the name of the mountain?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Does the name Debelo Brdo mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. But we --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just answer with a yes or no, please. If you can?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. This mountain, was it near your positions; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell this Chamber who held these positions on Debelo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much for brief answers, Witness, and we can continue in this way. You mentioned Colina Kapa, do you remember; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there just one Colina Kapa or are there more than one, could you please tell us?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: There is the observatory on Colina Kapa. There is one Colina Kapa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry. This name, can it be distinguished as Mala Colina Kapa and Velika Colina Kapa, the big Colina Kapa and the small Colina Kapa, is this it?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would like you to tell me if you can any other names of locations, elevated positions that apart from those that you mentioned in Sarajevo where Muslim troops were located, were positioned?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: From our side, as what I wanted to add, was the Mojmilo hill, which is throughout its length, and on the northern side, that was not our part of the front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, do you know the Zuc hill?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is on the northern side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know who held it?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Well, Zuc went from one hands into other hands. At the end Muslims held it, but I was not in that part of the front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: It was not within our reach.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. If I ask you if you know it, you can just answer with a yes or no, that would be good. In that case we will go much more quickly. Do you know the Hum hill, please, yes or nor?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the times you were in Sarajevo, in the Sarajevo area what forces occupied Hum?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, I'm going to go to another subject, the subject of instructions, did you ever receive, as a military person, instructions that came from your superiors, from your hierarchy, regarding civilians, yes or no, with respect to civilians, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: We were told in strict terms not to target anything of our own free will and that we were not supposed to fire at civilians, to hold on and respect Geneva Conventions and this went as a circular letter from the command and it was read before all the soldiers. And we were threatened by court-martials if we --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am going to interrupt you. I'm sorry, but I have to do it. You say that this was read to you. Could you tell us briefly what was read to you?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Mostly these circular letters, orders, contained two elements. First of all, was a recommendation of how we, as soldiers, should behave, as far as we were concerned on the inside, and these second part, contained how the Muslim side behaved, which we of course couldn't check. We were not able to check that but these were the two parts of such circular letters. And also that we were not supposed to respond in the way that they fired, for instance, if they did something which was not proper, we should not answer in the same way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Witness. You spoke of sanctions, but very briefly, could you tell us what you were told at the time regarding the sanctions?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: There was court-martial and it was in Zagrebacka Street, and the soldiers we founded unpleasant. I know there were some comrades who didn't like it and they rebelled because it was said that anybody who broke any rules would go before the court-martial. I believe there was a judge call Sipcic. I am not sure of this name. It was something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, since you say there was a judge then you gave his name and who was there, could you tell me, please, if you know, what could have happened if there were violations, and I am saying if there had been violations. It's hypothetical.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Probably according to the rules of military law. In the Army of Republika Srpska, I don't know of any such violations as far as we are concerned, as far as our side is concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Regarding the question -- I will come back to another point, but regarding the question of the ammunition, did you receive any instructions in terms of use of ammunition; yes or no? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: The instructions were --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes or no, Witness.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, very briefly, Witness, what were these instructions in relation to the use of ammunition?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: To start with, there were no such instructions, but later on from July onwards, it was ordered that ammunition should be saved, preserved, and particularly when we are talking about mortar shells, and they should be only in answering fire, in responding, in returning fire of Muslim fire because there were already a lack of ammunition, particularly of mortar shells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I am just going to do a brackets here. We will come back to this question. But you said "from our side." What do you mean? Could you tell us about what is your ethnic origin, could you tell us very briefly?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I am an atheist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's very well. That's for your faith. What about your culture?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I belong to the European culture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much for your answer. It is a perfect answer. I will come back to the question of ammunition now, Witness. You spoke of tanks. Your positions, were they ever shelled by tank fire or fired on by tank fire; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before the witness answers, although I encourage him --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not from the tanks, on the positions of mortar batteries, the infantry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Formally object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, I only see part of your objection in the transcript, and I was listening to the French channel, as a matter of fact. So could you please repeat, if possible, I think it is a rather technical procedural issue, in the presence of the witness your objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Leading, however the words have been put in the witness's mouth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. In general terms, asking for a yes or no very often results in leading questions. On the other hand, Mr. Stamp, if we try to find out whether the witness knows something -- well, knows about a certain subject, I would say that it would be a proper way of establishing. If you say, do you know about ever being shelled, yes or no, then that of course is not very leading. I mean, if you would have not have asked the witness to answer with a yes or no, the question would have been, I would say, appropriate. What Mr. Piletta-Zanin is seeking, as a matter of fact, is to get short answers. And I think that's, under the circumstances, not prohibited. Therefore, I noticed that, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, when you are touching upon subjects where we -- where the yes or the no would not lead the witness, but rather insist on short answers, I will allow you to do that. But please keep in mind that if we touch upon a subject where the yes or a no would result in leading the witness, you should refrain from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gladly, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I wasn't objecting necessarily or solely to the yes or no part, but solely: "Were your positions ever shelled by tank fire? " I submit that that is a leading question. He would have asked if they were attacked and by what, that would have been a way of going about very quickly without leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you are going to do without leading, you should do that. On the other hand, whether positions were ever attacked, yes, I think the witness has testified already that several positions were attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. I am just going to go to another subject.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke to us about these mobile mortars, you called them F-A-P, Fap. And they were mounted on the platforms for firing, do you remember that, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With what frequency these military vehicles fired from Muslim positions when you, obviously, you were stationed in the Sarajevo area?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: To start with, on a daily basis during a particular period during the day, I said that we more or less registered or recorded their firing, and we already knew during which period of time they would operate, they would fire. And they had that very precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. These objects, were they very mobile; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, were you, yourself, or members of your unit, were you able to see these objects when weapons were fired from the opposing side?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. On two occasions I saw that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. How many times were you able to see this?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Personally, twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Since you saw that on two occasions, next to which object and what I mean is facility, building, another thing, where these objects were stationed from which the fire was opened?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Left to the Kosevo tunnel, west from the Kosevo tunnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it near houses? Was it in an urban area or any other?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, do you personally know persons, military or civilian, who may have been wounded as a result of the attack which -- attacks firing which was launched from these mobile objects?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: No. No, not in this case. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In general, do you know people or persons who were injured as a result of a shell attack?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Were these military people or civilians? What can you tell us, very briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Soldiers, in this case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, when you tell us about the firing that originated from the other side, and when the attacks occurred, what can you tell us about the number of shells which landed on your positions?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I told you that they didn't fire more than two or three projectiles on different positions, so mostly it would be one or two that would land during a certain period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You just told us that you -- they didn't fire more than two or -- and what did you then say? You said two --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two to four, two from two different weapons. And correction, that would be when they were not attacking and when they were attacking, then it would be more intense. That was what was permanent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I heard on the French channel two to 4, where I see on the English channel two or three.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, so your testimony is that when the battery opened fire one would expect four successive firing in a very brief period of time, grenades falling in a very brief period of time. Is that how we are to understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am going to rephrase it. You are talking about two to four shots, are you talking about salvo? Are you saying when the opposing side opened fire was it in salvos or was it two, three, four firing, close together?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were in hurry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Why were they in a hurry?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Because we opened fire on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Are you telling us that you returned fire, you opened fire in response to enemy fire?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. According to what you were taught, militarily, is it legitimate to open fire in response, to return fire even when it came from the city?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: For me, that's normal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, now I would like to come back to another line of questioning.
