Could You please tell me if your battalion, as far as you know, had ever, since you were in charge of mortars, had ever destroyed a cultural facilities or symbolic facilities? For instance, highly religious facilities or objects.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to come back to the area of Grbavica, please. What was the route that you had to take if, say, a civilian was wounded, hypothetically speaking, in such-and-such a hospital, what were the routes, open routes, please, bearing in mind the neighbourhood that you knew, Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, since the Muslim positions were also in Debelo Brdo all these routes was covered by snipers and so on. The only thing that was safe, soldiers in trenches were safe, that is, in the houses on the front line. This route was the route which is even used today, alongside Vraca. So when we are talking about bringing out our wounded, it would be alongside Vraca and then there was a coffee restaurant, shop called Stana and then there would be a route across Trebevic, and it was always covered by snipers, exposed to snipers. So we had to use deviation through Tvrdimici and Mount Jahorina. Our first hospital was in Pale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, what you tell us here, is this also valid for the civilians? You spoke about soldiers who were wounded, but what happened to civilians, please?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you spoke to us of snipers. How did you react, how did you respond, militarily speaking, to a sniper attack, if you were able to react, to respond, very briefly, please?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: We tried to just speed up in a vehicle that we were in, to drive more quickly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. This is a strategy of acceleration, that is fleeing, escape. But if you had attacks against you, in principle, in general, how were you reacting to the risk, to the danger opposed by sniper nests? Did you try and take them out to eliminate them?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was fire opened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you know if sniper positions, whoever they were targeting on your positions, did they exist in other locations apart from the mount that you mentioned earlier?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could you tell us, precisely if you know, what were these locations? And I am of course talking about the BH side.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Colina Kapa, Debelo Brdo, as you said. Those snipers were on the opposite side of the Miljacka river, positioned on the Executive Council building. The former BH Assembly building. The Holiday Inn Hotel --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Slowly please, for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: As I was saying, on the Executive Council building, the Assembly building of the former Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Holiday Inn Hotel, on the Bristol Hotel, positions on prominent buildings, on the north bank of the Miljacka river. And they were pointing directly towards our positions so that it was very dangerous to take the transit route via Vraca, and our only route was up the Vraca Street, that's how we called it. I don't know the real name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you just spoke about high-rise buildings and those high-rise buildings, what could you tell us about them? Were they military buildings? Civilian buildings? Official buildings? Apartment buildings or whatever?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: There were no military buildings there. These were mostly high-rise buildings and large apartment buildings, and the hotels that I mentioned, and the assembly and the Executive Council, that is buildings of prewar political institutions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the frequency with which these nests were used, of course, during the period that you spent in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Nonstop.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Perhaps before we go into asking the witness about frequency a foundation can be laid. Because we are hearing the witness was posted well in Sarajevo at positions, one out of the range of 120-millimetre mortar of 6.000 metres and another at 3.500 metres. If perhaps this personal knowledge could be inquired upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like this objection to be formally rejected for the following reason: Is that is what this witness said and knew is that he couldn't use such a route because it was under fire, one increased the speed. So one could deduce from that that he was familiar with the phenomenon and that it is quite factual his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At least when he was driving in a car by and if you are talking about frequency, of course, you might -- could you -- no, the objection is -- well, you give an explanation of why the witness knows and that is an explanation that could be the right one and could perhaps explain part of the objection, but perhaps not all of it. Could I ask you, when you answered that question about the nonstop use of the sniper nests, could you please tell us how, on the basis of what, you can tell us that it was nonstop used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the basis of personal experience, because whatever moved was targeted. And the positions of our forces was something that I personally toured as an observer. And I was warned by our members of the army that as we crossed from one trench to another or one building to another, where we should run across without hesitating, without stopping because they knew from where our troops were being attacked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand you well that whenever you moved in that area from one position to another one, snipers were always active, at least you took that into account that they were active all the time. Is that how I have to understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke to us a moment ago about the official buildings of the Presidency. Could you describe that building very briefly? Was it a ground floor building or did it have several storeys or whatever?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: You probably mean the Executive Council, not the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. We are talking about the Executive Council. You are quite right.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: It is a dominant building in the part of Sarajevo known as Marijn Dvor, behind the Vrbanja bridge. I think it has 13 floors, I am not 100 per cent certain of that, but I think it has 13 storeys and it is dominant in relation to our positions in Miljacka and Vraca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us, if you know personally, how this building was used during the period you spent there? Was it used for strictly civilian purposes or, vice versa, for military purposes?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: It was not used at all for civilian purposes. That is where the snipers were positioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I said that when I visited our positions down there, the first warning I received was to take shelter whenever I was exposed to the view from the building of the Executive Council. And I personally experienced on two occasions next to the school, the Radojka Latic school, you can feel the bullet. It doesn't whistle, but because it's so close, you feel it whizzing by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, since you are talking about the snipers, what can you tell us in connection with that problem, regarding the fears, the apprehensions of the civilian population living in Grbavica, if you know, of course? But very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Objection, irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will rephrase my question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke about your visits. Did you -- do you know whether there were special structures in place to allow you to move and be less exposed to danger?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Very briefly, those protection structures for your army, what did they consist of?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: There would be a driver, an escort, somebody who would guide us to our positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there any fixed means of protection and not mobile ones?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Some sort of screens were put up to screen from view. They weren't really obstacles that could prevent a bullet from going through, but there was such screens at Vraca and Zlatiste and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This type of protection that you have just mentioned, were they also used to protect the civilian population, this type of barriers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue this line of questioning, we heard a lot of evidence on these issues. And is this contested by the Prosecution that such -- that such screens or other ways of protecting either military or civilians did exist on the Serbian-held side?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Not contested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the -- especially when it is not contested, unless it has a specific meaning, as we heard one of the last days in respect of specific lines of view. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke to us a moment ago about buildings of cultural or strategic importance in Sarajevo. Did you imply within that group, museums, for instance, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, according to your personal experience and concerning the events that occurred on the opposing side, what could you tell us in connection with museums that you know from personal experience?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: We did not target those facilities, but I could mention an example. After the Marshal Tito Barracks was captured, when the Muslim side at the beginning of June, I think it was in June, took control of that barracks, sometime around then into the yard of the National Museum in Sarajevo, it is a big building and in the middle there is a garden. And something targeted us, fire was opened on our positions. And our scouts couldn't establish what it was. And they called us in to see what it was, and in our judgment, we established that into that yard of the museum, in the middle, we couldn't see that because it is impossible to see from our positions, a mortar, a 120-millimetre mortar had been positioned there which had opened fire from that position on the targets on our side, at Vraca, and one shell even hit our position in Ivanici, and we wanted to respond but we received orders not to open fire on such facilities and later on they also stopped firing from there because we didn't respond.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have a purely procedural problem. Will you please take off your headphones and put them in front of you and don't look at the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Don't look at the screen

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I also ask whether the witness would put on his headphones again. [Interpretation] Do you understand French?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you then please take care that the transcript is not on the screen of the witness and ask him to take his headphones off.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have some interruptions in my headphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you take them off. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if I make this objection, it is because I think I heard in one of the two languages that I am listening to and it is not English, the word "stela" which is a tombstone. When one knows the importance that the Prosecution attaches to shelling of cemeteries and funerals, I must say that I don't see in the English transcript the word "stela." There is the mention of the garden.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask the interpreters whether they heard the word just -- I see some nodding. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then could we -- do I understand that this was used when the witness described the courtyard?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was very fast, and he mentioned something being in the middle of the courtyard. I think so. "Stela."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please put on your headphones again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is extremely difficult for me to follow what I have to do. And I am really -- I really do apologise to the interpreters. And ask them to be precise to use all the words used, and that all the words should be found in the transcript, be it English or French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Mr. Piletta-Zanin, in the answer of the interpreters, they also said that it went very very quickly. So I take it that the interpreters do their utmost best to translate every single word they hear, and at the same time they have a very difficult task if one is speaking too quickly. Could you please put on your headphones again. We had a small problem. The interpreters did not catch the word "stela" you used as being in the courtyard -- in the court of the museum. This is also caused because of the speed with which you and Mr. Piletta-Zanin are speaking. So may I, again, ask you to slow down so that the interpreters can follow you. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke to us about instructions that were given to you not to respond to these provocative shots. Who were the -- who were the person or persons who gave you those instructions? Could you tell this Chamber that?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: The chief of artillery, Grajic told us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, did you respect those instructions; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, you mentioned a moment ago the Kosevo hill. Is that the same name that is given to the hospital, Kosevo Hospital; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, only it is on the other side of the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So when speaking of the Kosevo Hospital and the problems linked to the artillery, could you tell us anything on the basis of your personal experience, please? I am referring to the whole of the Kosevo area.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: So the Kosevo hill is to the left of the road to Vogosca. The football stadium is there too, and the Kosevo sports centre. And on the right-hand side are the hospital facilities, on the east. The hospital facilities which cover a large area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. But my question was, do you know whether fire was ever opened from the area known as the Kosevo Hospital area?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, first of all, your question to the witness was not whether they ever received fire fired from the Kosevo hospital, but you asked him whether he could tell anything on the basis of his personal experience about the whole of the Kosevo area. So that is not -- and your next question was leading. So would you refrain from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know where the Kosevo Hospital is situated; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. The whole hospital complex.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you describe for us very briefly this complex?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: The complex begins with macillo school of medicine, traumatology, it is a large complex of several buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you say, it is hundreds of metres or one kilometre? How large is it in area?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: It is about 800 metres long, and about 100 metres wide.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, what could you tell us regarding this zone that we are speaking of, and concerning the war itself, what you yourself knew about it?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: They used that complex too, to fire at our positions, not always, but during some kind of a ceasefire when they wanted us to respond. And we had strict instructions not to respond. So they would use a mortar shot or some provocative fire was opened most frequently at times of signed ceasefires.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you indicate the type of military targets that you targeted in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: In addition to those that I have mentioned, that is their artillery positions, we also hit the centres where they rallied their infantry forces and from which they attacked our positions, and that is, in the first place, the Jewish cemetery. Their positions on the other side of the Miljacka river, around the bridge called Brotherhood and Unity, where they frequently tried to break through our lines, then their forces were also amassing in a school and we had a report, it was in Buca Potok, around the Pero Kosoric square and around the Viktor Bubanj barracks where particularly at the beginning they continually sought to capture the barracks, and on the map I think it was the Hrasno settlement, I think. I am not too sure about that. I would be able to tell you better on a map. And Pavle Goranin settlement, and of course the Mojmilo hill. In addition to what I already said, that is, Zlatiste, Debelo Brdo, Colina Kapa, and of course the Kosevo complex.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. You mentioned a school --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you how much time you would still need approximately, because I -- if possible, I would try and see whether we could conclude with this witness today just short before the weekend. How much time would you still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, at this rhythm and without further interruptions, three minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you finish by 12.00. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, very quickly, yes or no, please, you mentioned a school a moment ago. Do you know whether that school was emptied of its civilian occupants; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, with regard to what is known as the cemetery called Jewish, this cemetery itself -- I am not talking about the zone, but the cemetery itself enclosed within its walls, to what side did it belong at the time that you were there?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: It was in between. It was a zone in between. We were to the west and the Muslim positions were to the east. This separated us, the distance being 15 to 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're just telling me, Witness, that the cemetery itself used as termed was a buffer zone between the two armies; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, but let me clarify. We didn't enter the Jewish cemetery at all, and the Muslims did use it to attack our positions. They used the monuments as personal protection and shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And my very last question in two parts: Was there a synagogue at the bottom of the so-called Jewish cemetery, a chapel?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: A chapel, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And this building that you call "chapel," which force occupied it, if any?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: No one held it. It was closer to our positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions, Mr. President. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stamp, I take it that you would have a possibility to address the Chamber, perhaps better in the absence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Notwithstanding it will be very brief --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you, Mr. Usher, to escort the witness out of the courtroom just for a short while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We received in September the summary for this witness and it was very brief, and with your leave, Mr. President, I think it ought to be placed on the record because we are going to ask that some sort of remedy be imposed. "The witness was a member of reserve JNA forces and as a member of the Rogatica battalion he participated in support of JNA units in protection of barracks in Faletici." May I indicate that Faletici is north-west of the centre of Sarajevo city. "This was when JNA in April and at the beginning of May tried to protect soldiers at military --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, could you please slow down. That is what the interpreters ask us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The reference to Faletici when it goes on: "When JNA in April and beginning of May tried to protect soldiers at military service as well as the material means in surrounding barracks by Muslim paramilitary formations. At the beginning of May, his unit was disposed in the area of Lukavica and Vraca where he was a witness of Muslim attacks with infantry weapons and ABiH sniping attacks from the building of the Executive Council, Bristol Hotel, Holiday Inn Hotel."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I apologise, but it cannot be read at this speed. It's impossible to follow. We don't have a text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Give a reading to me ask then I will read it slowly for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I will read it reasonably slow as of now. "At the beginning of May his unit was disposed in the area of Lukavica and Vraca where he was a witness of Muslim attacks with infantry weapons and ABiH sniping attacks from the building of Executive Council, Bristol Hotel, Holiday Inn Hotel, against the positions of his unit on separation line, Vrbanja Bridge-Zlatiste." Observations. It makes no reference of the major part of his testimony which involves mortaring, being in a mortar position and observing mortar positions. Second observation, it indicates that the position of his unit was at the Vrbanja Bridge-Zlatiste which is on the Miljacka river. We are -- we learned today that his units were positioned in Petrovici and Ivanici many kilometres from the centre of Sarajevo. My learned colleague said that he had indicated that the witnesses would give general evidence about a variety of things. The letter I have seen as translated which is a long letter and it would not serve any purpose to read it, merely indicates, and not in respect to this particular named witnesses, but in respect to other witnesses, it indicates generally that the witnesses may testify about a whole host of matters listed which occupied more than one page. There is no way, it is submitted, Mr. President, that we can prepare for any witness with this type of summary. And I raise it because we are going to have another week, next week, I know the remedy could not be that this witness will be stopped from testifying, however, I would ask that precise directions be given to the Defence in respect to these summaries so that proper preparations can be made in respect to them. There is one worrying part, and I am quite sure it was not an intended thing from Defence, but there seems to be a misdescription when he says that his unit was on the Miljacka river and we find that it was thousands of kilometres away. That is what I ask the court and perhaps issue directions as to the nature of these summaries. What is worse is that we did write the Defence asking them for further and better particulars because we could not see the relevance of the indictment issues from this summary. And they did send a later summary which was not any more helpful and subsequently another summary which was in the same terms as what I just read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The objection is not the first time that we hear this objection. I would rather first conclude the testimony of this witness and we will see whether -- I don't know how much time you would think you would need, Mr. Stamp. What I want to prevent is that because of procedural battles, that we have to hurry when we examine a witness, which is always a bad thing to do. How much time do you think you would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I will try, but I could not guarantee that I will be finish by the close of today's proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you think that it might be possible to conclude today, I would rather give an opportunity to Mr. Piletta-Zanin to respond after we finished with this witness. Let's first see how far we come. Yes. Mr. Usher, could you please escort -- yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I do not wish to respond, but I must mention something. I said on two occasions, and once I believe in your office, but I said it earlier, I told earlier to the representatives of the Prosecution that our letter was generic and that for all the soldiers, we will do the same. I just said it before the intervention of Mr. Stamp by saying that knowing very well, and now, as if my intervention never happened, and this was done in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You may escort the witness into the courtroom. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I do agree that you indicated that you would do the same. Finally, I think it is up to the Chamber to give guidance to the parties of what they are expected to do. We will consider the matter at a later stage and what we will also do is carefully, perhaps then compare the summaries with what actually was the testimony of the witness and see whether this is relevant for any guidance or decision to be taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stamp. You will now be examined by counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could I please have the transcript on the screen in English?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think there is no reason to deny you access to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, the most important thing for you to look at the transcript as specifically is, that you stop talking when the text is still moving. Don't try to read too much and try to concentrate on the questions and on your answers, rather than checking the transcript. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the first time you spoke to any member of the Defence team about your testimony in this case?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Sometime in May this year, that is 2002, there was Mrs. Prodanovic from Srbinje and earlier we had had a contact in relation with the post in the company that I worked for and she wanted to meet me and talk to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You met her for the first time in May of this year, is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I didn't meet her for the first time in May. We met before in Rogatica at the court between the court case, between the post office in Rogatica and the transport company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am going to ask you to listen, Witness, very carefully to what I ask and answer simply to what I ask. I didn't ask about the circumstances in which you met or where it was that you met. I want to know when was the first time, when?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: In May. In relation to this testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you meet her before May in relation to anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there is a mistake in the transcript and I have to state it. I believe that what was said in the answer of the witness, there was the segment that should have come before the question that I am reading at the moment, 63.14, I believe that the question of Mr. Stamp was [In English] "When was the first time" [Interpretation] et cetera and so on in relation to this testimony and so on. And it is the other way around. This is not what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but it was a response to what the witness -- let me just ask you. When did you for the first time meet Ms. Prodanovic, for the first time in your life?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was sometime in June, in June, in the summer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the first time you met her ever in your life, 2001?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And that was at court. She was the lawyer for the opposing side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you then discuss testimony to be given in The Hague or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. We just -- we just spoke to each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When did you for the first time speak with Ms. Prodanovic on a potential testimony in this court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In May 2002. In 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please try to give your answers just as you did it right away. Listen carefully to the answer, answer the question, and if further information is needed, you certainly will be asked for. Please proceed, Mr. Mundis. [Sic]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you spoke about this case in May 2002, did you give her a statement which was taken in writing?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I am sorry. I seem to be having interference and I didn't hear this question at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please assist and see whether there is -- whether it is the line or the headphone. If there will be again interference, please tell me so that we can try to fix it. Is it better now? Please proceed, Mr. Mundis [sic]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you met and spoke with her about this case in May 2002, did you give a written statement to her?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you give a written statement to any member of the Defence team in respect to your testimony before today?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was this?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: 11th or 12th of September in Rogatica in 2002.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you gave that written statement, did you tell the Defence about what you were occupied with doing in Sarajevo in 1992?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell them about your experience as a mortar man in Ivanici?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell them about your experience as mortar man in Petrovici?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to take you to your experiences in Sarajevo. Firstly, you have told us that you experienced sniping when you were travelling in the vicinity of the Miljacka river. Where were you travelling to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is not the testimony of this witness, that he was fired at when --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It misrepresents the testimony of the witness, Mr. Stamp. Would you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when you experienced sniping in the Grbavica area?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Most frequently I witnessed the positions in a vehicle which brought food to our soldiers on the front line. The driver of that vehicle was Mico Obradovic from Rogatica --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am going to ask you again to listen to the question and just answer it simply. So you travelled on a vehicle to Rogatica which was delivering food; is that what you are saying? Sorry, to Grbavica, which was delivering food, is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you travel from your -- the positions where your mortar units were located?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Occasionally. Not always.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your role on that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: To visit and to find out about our positions of our infantry and fortifying these -- or -- no.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter corrects herself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Establishing the positions from which the Muslims were firing, which means they were reconnaissance tasks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the vicinity of the river, the Miljacka river in Grbavica, you were able to see the positions from where the Muslims were firing?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question isn't very clear, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can I first hear your -- again your answer -- you answered the question. Could you repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. From the front side, from the frontal positions on the Miljacka side. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, not all of them. It was impossible to see all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your mortar unit have a target commander?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Well, he didn't choose targets, he only received orders and passed them on to be carried out when there was firing. So he was the battery commander. He did not himself determine, he didn't decide on the targets himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From --

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: May I add?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, you may not. You answered the question. From whom did he receive his commands to fire at targets?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Most frequently from the chief of artillery and also from the commander of the battalion in emergency situations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the chief of artillery and the commander of the battalion have units that were responsible to observe and locate the targets?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did your battery crew use map coordinates to fire on these targets?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. But most of the time on the map you cannot see the height of the building or where the fire is coming from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from going to Grbavica during this conflict, apart from accompanying persons delivering food, did you go there with any other group of persons?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of Vlasko in respect to the Jewish cemetery? Aleksic?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever met him?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your units in the Grbavica area cooperate with him and his units in the defence of the Bosnian Serb positions?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. At the time he was located somewhere to -- more southern from us. South of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you coordinate with Aleksic with respect to attacks on Bosnian Muslim positions?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: No. Not we personally. Perhaps he gave some targets that were then determined and decided on by the chief of artillery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where Aleksic got his ammunition from?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was his commander, if any, in the Bosnian Serb Army?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I don't know, but I think he only had his Chetnik unit that was independent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you said you don't know?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what way did you cooperate with Aleksic in the defence of the Serb cause, so to speak, could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Personally. We were just on the same side. There was no cooperation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The commander of the Rogatica Battalion, was that Rajko Kusic?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the battalion?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Radomir Furtula, former captain of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Rajko Kusic --

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I am sorry. Radomir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, since these names will be very useful for us later on in the further examination, it would be good if it was correctly put in the transcript, the first one wasn't mentioned, and the second one isn't put in correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second one is Radomir Furtula.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Rajko Kusic a commander of any unit or any military formation that you know about?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Sometime in May there was conflict in Rogatica and Rajko became the commander of the Rogatica Brigade, light Rogatica Brigade which had nothing to do with us. Rajko belonged to a different corps. The middle of October that was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Your battalion was formally a part of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps until October, is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after October you were subordinated to another corps?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a corps or a brigade you were subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: As part of the Zvornik Corps, but it was the Rogatica Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was Rajko Kusic the commander of the Rogatica Brigade?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive commands to fire at tanks?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Once, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's be certain about that. "Once, perhaps," what does that mean? Did you or did you not receive any command to fire at tanks with your mortars?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: We received the order then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I take it from your answer is that you received commands to fire at tanks on at least one occasion?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. But it is obvious that mortar shells can't do much because what has to be used there is cumulative and not instant highly explosive ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I take it from your answer that it will not be militarily useful to fire the mortar at the tank, you will not achieve a military purpose if you fire the mortar at the tank; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object to this question. I object to this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you take your headphones off, please, and could -- Mr. Usher, could you switch off the transcript. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I object to this question for the simple reason that there could be many ways of using a tank with an open territory --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we have an objection expressed in terms which does not indicate any answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please make your objection such that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. There are many ways of using such-and-such a weapon, such-and-such a mean, theoretically, this could be protected, or it could be -- I just wanted to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The beginning of your objection, your explanation to the objection is that the question is perhaps not clear or that different answers could be given to that question. If you object against the question, you should use the terms, say, well, the question is not clear or it could be given different answers, so in an abstract way and not going into the matter itself. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I never said that I was objecting because the question wasn't clear. I never said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I want on abstract terms the type of objection you are raising.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The way the question was phrased isn't normal. What should be asked is in which different situations, we can have all different situations where use of such-and-such a weapon is perfectly legitimate. So is there such-and-such a weapon that was opposed to him. So in a general terms this question is not acceptable because it can imply many many different answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mainly, questions should not be given possibility to give different answers -- let me just go back to the question now. The -- [Interpretation] The witness introduced by himself the subject which is in the question at the moment, and perhaps you could proceed, Mr. Stamp. [In English] Well, perhaps after we finish this part of the transcript. So in 15 seconds you may put on the transcript again. Not at this very moment. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was asking Mr. Golic if I can take it from what you said earlier that there was no military purpose in trying to neutralizing a tank with mortar fire, is that a correct understanding of your evidence?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: No. My expertise isn't up to that level, militarily speaking, but the tanks were dug in and you could only fire with shells which had fuses that were not instant, but that were delayed, but mostly we didn't receive this order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that persons on your side of the lines, and including yourself -- withdrawn. Is it your evidence that persons on your side of the line including yourself could see the movement of these one 120-millimetre mortars in the vicinity of the railway tracks?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in Kosevo they could be seen?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, even better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have communications in the area of your mortar battery by way of field phone? Did you use field phones to communicate between your mortar battery and your observers?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Only in the battery, and we had hand-held phones for urgent communications in the case of a Muslim attack to be able to communicate with those at the Jewish cemetery, but they were very rarely used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your mortar batteries were able to fire on these artillery weapons in Sarajevo while they were being set up?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. I don't understand. While they were adjusted? What? I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your answer --

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: When they were active?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I understand your evidence to be that you could see them as they moved and before they fired; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, looking at the clock, I don't know, could you when you move to your next subject indicate so we then could have a break. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Maybe I could ask --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Maybe I could move on to another subject briefly as there may be something that we need to check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you know there are certain limitations as far as the tapes are concerned, so please proceed and try to find out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you moved to Petrovici, what were your targets from Petrovici?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Quite different targets. The area of Debelo Brdo, Colina Kapa and Zlatiste and below that. The rest was not within our range. And anyway we opened fire very rarely because SFOR was there already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what I wanted to ask about. Do you mean SFOR or do you mean UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: UNPROFOR in those days, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These were UNPROFOR military observers?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. And they came to the separation lines and they regularly toured our positions and checked whether there was any firing in relation to the previous day in Petrovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, notwithstanding the fact that UNPROFOR were there, you did fire but more -- but less frequently? I take it --

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I said very rarely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was because of the presence of UNPROFOR military observers?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: No. Our lines had already been -- become stabilised and probably some other battery fired in front of the Jewish cemetery. I don't know that. But anyway, only in the case that we were fired upon from Debelo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just asked you if you fired only very rarely only because of the presence of UNPROFOR observers, and your answer was "no." May I ask you this as a last question: Did you say in answer to your own counsel: "Our battery didn't really operate because observers from SFOR had already arrived." Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object. That is absolutely not what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am asking him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, this is the question. You cannot answer the question for the witness. If you object to a question, of course, you are allowed to do so, but not by indicating what the answer should be and that the question is wrong. I will check that during the break. If there is any reason to say that you would not agree that this is what the witness said or did not say, first of all, we can easily check that in the tapes. So if you would like to check that, please do so. If there is any reason to do so, even the Chamber might do it. But this is not the way you can interfere in cross-examination. Mr. Stamp, please repeat the question. And may I ask you not to refer to counsel as "your counsel" because --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. And I do apologise for that. That was out of place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Question, sir, yes or no, did you say this, did you say: "Our battery didn't really operate because observers from SFOR had already arrived. They had regularly visited our positions. They were familiar with things, so that our operations were much rarer and far between." The question is: Did you say so?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Not quite like that. It is very important in this case that we didn't not open fire only because UNPROFOR was there. So it wasn't the only reason. Even the English RAF had been there, we would have opened fire if our lines had been attacked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, are there other questions? I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There are other questions but we could perhaps take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will have a break until 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would rather whatever problems there might be, I would rather continue at this very moment to see how far we come with the witness and if there is any other issue relating to time or whatever, we can address that later. Let's see how far we can come. Mr. Usher, can you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, if you could clarify the issue as to your service in the Sarajevo theatre. Do you remember the date that your unit left the Sarajevo theatre?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Between the 15th and 20th of October, but one company had already left before that around the 10th of October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that period, the 15th to the 20th of October, did your unit return for action in the Sarajevo theatre at any time after?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was your unit transferred from Ivanici to Petrovici?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Sometime in July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is in 1992?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: In July -- not June. July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and that is in 1992, is it?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In respect to Aleksic, you said that perhaps he gave some targets that were then determined and decided on by the chief of artillery. About when was this?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Probably when he was attacked. He had his own 82-millimetre mortar and if he was attacked and he needed fire to be opened from artillery, he may have requested it. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, was that before or after you moved from Ivanici to Petrovici?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: In both periods he was there and he stayed there and he was there when we arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those targets that he might have given in the vicinity of the Jewish cemetery?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. He was there. No, I am afraid I just don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did your unit or battery ever fire mortars which hit civilians?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: No, not intentionally, that's for certain. Only military targets were fired at. I do not exclude the possibility of an error.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your battery have an observer who could tell you where your shots landed?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Not always. In emergencies there wasn't time to go to the observation post, but fire would be opened when they attacked. And those targets were usually determined in advance on the basis of the knowledge of our people in positions, the azimuth would be taken, the rough distance and then corrections were -- only corrections were made later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said it was normal for you to respond to fire from the city; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that civilians lived in the city?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: We knew the city was there. How many of them had left, how many stayed behind --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say how accurate was your mortar crew when the fired into the city?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: We had extensive preparations in March 1992. The mortar battery was left without a crew because before the war, 70 per cent of the manpower consisted of members of the Muslim faith.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say how accurate --

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: And let me finish, please. And we had test firing in Kalinovik on the 26th of March and at that test, after 15 days of training in those conditions, precision proved to be extremely good. However upon arriving in Sarajevo and particularly at a later stage, we ran out of light instant highly explosive mines of 13 kilograms so that mortar shells started arriving which were intended for older mortars of 48. These were repaired shells from Pretis, from Vogosca, unpainted shells coming directly off the factory belts and using different fuses so that one could not always guarantee this. And there were especially shells with different gunpowder charges of older production which had been in warehouses for a long time and all this affected precision. As regards the crew, I think that the crews, in view of the short period of time, were very well trained but other factors of a more technical character certainly affected the precision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about yourself, you speak of the crew. May I ask you this: Did you ever boast to anyone or tell anyone that you could put a mortar round down a chimney? You could fire a mortar round at a chimney and put it down that chimney, did you ever tell anyone that?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: But let me explain if I may. I appeal to Your Honours to allow this. In the Serbian people, particularly in these different times, legends develop. 90 per cent of them are untrue, and I never said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you the subject of a legend?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: No. It was more like propaganda and intimidation of the opposing side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. We will speak about that later. Could you fire a mortar at a chimney and hit it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President,.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I object for the precision more so as we know, that in Sarajevo there are different types of chimneys and this word used could signify many things and I think we need to be very precise about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question has been answered, the objection is denied. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you are firing at a target within the city, you yourself and your crew with a good reliable 120 millimetre round --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Just a minute, Mr. Stamp. The problem is the answer does not appear in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I could just repeat the question. I remember the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think everyone heard as his answer, I take it, that the answer was "no." There seems to be no doubt about that. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you are in possession of a reliable 120 millimetre round, could you fire at a target with that round and hit the target?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: In the case of a 120 millimetre mortar, any hit within a circle of 50 metres is considered a hit. It can be a chimney, something a metre by a metre, but what is a target can be hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: But in view of all the different circumstances...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I take it that your answer means that you could hit a target within an area of 50 metres?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were firing rounds into the city where you know civilians resided, knowing and believing that these rounds were unreliable; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: In principle, yes. But we thought that they were reliable. Probably if I hadn't behaved in that way, I wouldn't be here to testify today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you saw mortars moving in the vicinity of a rail track and in the area of Kosevo. Let us begin with the vicinity of the rail track. You said that was in Velecici?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Velecici, behind the station, the track toward Velecici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw that mortar moving on these tracks, where were you?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Slightly to the east at Vraca, close to the memorial park in a prominent position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By "prominent" I take it you were on high ground where you could see clearly the area that you were looking at?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What distance did you see this mortar being moved? In other words, from where you first saw it being moved to where you saw it stop, what was the distance?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Well, it's a very short distance, perhaps 50 metres. He would go from outside behind of the station building and then he would move back in the same way as it came out, in the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of energy was used to move this vehicle? And when I say "energy" was it an engine, was it a jet, was it human, was it an animal, what was the mode of force used to move this vehicle?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: It was mounted on a railway truck. How it moved, we couldn't see. You couldn't see the engine. Whether there was an engine and separate machine which it could move one of vehicles. In any case, it moved at this very short distance. It would come out and fire and on that occasion I only saw one round.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw the -- well let me ask you, did you say you saw 120 millimetre mortars being moved in the Kosevo area?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: In front of the tunnel, the Kosevo tunnel. I don't mean the Kosevo itself, but the Kosevo tunnel on the rail -- on the freight, freight truck, Fap-13.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see it being moved from?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: From the tunnel, from the tunnel. So it would come out of the tunnel, it would then fire for a short while and then it would go back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where would it fire from?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: From a very short distance. So it is enough to come out of the tunnel, 20, 30 metres and then it would go back. All vehicles again they were mounted on -- it wasn't a transport case, but these were probably some freight vehicles for transporting timber or something and that was then removed, so it was a flatbed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your understanding, I take it, is that you were firing at these vehicles that you speak of? Is it your understanding that you would be given commands to return the fire to these vehicles that you saw moving?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I apologise. I apologise. But I just wondering whether the tone of the voice could be lower, pleased. This is very surprising to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I apologise. It was not meant to intimidate. Just to speed up the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp raised his voice but as he explained, it happened accidentally. Could you answer the question that he has put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I watched it we couldn't respond because I was there. We took the coordinates we saw where it was and then our scouts would wait the following day, the following days and it would be repeated in a certain period of time. And then we waited and we took the coordinates when it appeared and we were ready to fire, and then we would respond during the fire being fired. But when we were there, I was not on the battery position, but I did say that the communication means with the battery and there on the positions, for instance, like RUPs, we used them very rarely because in terms of city combat, these were not safe. They were not encoded. So very often they would be able to intercept our communication so we used them very rarely. Muslims had all the decoding devices and monitoring devices, listening devices.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you, by that explanation, saying that this RUP communications device would not be used to tell you that a mortar was coming out on the rail track because it might have been decoded?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what you are saying. Very well. So I take it -- or let me ask you this: Was it not possible to fire on those mortars that were moving distances of 30 to 50 metres before they had fired at you instead of responding to fire? Wasn't it possible, bearing in mind that you say that this had become a routine?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I said that later on, on these targets, at certain periods of time, we then noted when they appeared and we used preventive fire and I am not saying that we didn't do that later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are saying now that you used preventive fire once they were observed moving?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, up until the time you left Sarajevo, your units or the positions from which you fired were able to suppress the fire of these mortars and were not responding to the fire of these mortars?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: No. I said they were not within our range as soon as we moved to Petrovici, and it is not what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The mortars from Ivanici could fire at those targets, according to you, which moved in the vicinity of the railroad, could they not?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those that were moving in the vicinity of the tunnel at Kosevo, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, having regard to all your evidence could I take it to be correct that by the time you left Sarajevo the mortars from Ivanici would have been in a position to fire on to those targets as soon as those targets started to emerge from where they were coming?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: In Ivanici we were replaced by the 2nd battery consisting of people from Sarajevo --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. There is a time factor here. We are trying to economise on time. All I want to know is whether or not it was possible for the batteries at Ivanici and those batteries within range of Kosevo area near the tunnel, and the railroad track where you saw these moving vehicles, to fire -- to suppress these moving targets as they came out to fire? Was it possible? You nodded.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: It was possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that, to your knowledge, there was firing from the compound of the Kosevo Hospital complex.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You said you received orders not to return the fire, correct, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was during a truce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will have to clarify that. According to you, how many times during your stint in Sarajevo was there fire from the Kosevo Hospital complex?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, at least ten times, perhaps even 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: When I said -- I am sorry. But I said it is a very large complex from the Krajl Tomislav Street until Bijelava.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me again. You have told us 10 to 15 times. That is the answer to the question. Thank you. And I am just trying to press on quickly. Were there these occasions being 10 to 15 at times of a truce?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: To my knowledge, yes. I was on one occasion present and I saw it with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your evidence is, I take it, that you don't know of any occasion of at least 10 to 15 that you know of, when fire emanated from the Kosevo Hospital complex, when it was not in times of a truce?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I don't know whether the time when it wasn't truce, whether this happened. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you received these orders not to return fire, did you receive them only during these truce times?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive orders to return fire into the complex when there was no truce?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: We didn't receive such an order. We didn't receive an order to return fire. And I didn't say -- I don't know whether there was fire when it wasn't truce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just to clarify your evidence. You said, according to what I have here, "we didn't receive an order to return fire." Can I understand you to mean that you never at any time received an order to return fire into the Kosevo Hospital complex?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of any other mortar or artillery crew to the south of the city of Sarajevo that received orders to fire into the Kosevo Hospital complex?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of any mortar or artillery crew to the south of Sarajevo firing into the hospital complex at any time while you were in the Sarajevo area?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: No. I said that in previous questions, I don't know --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please. Again, do you know of any mortar or artillery unit positioned south of the city of Sarajevo that fired into the city? Sorry, that fired into Kosevo Hospital complex?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: No. I have no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you eventually become a mortar battery commander?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: No, just a commanding officer of the platoon, of the 2nd platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was this? Year, month, day, if you can.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Already in Sarajevo I was the commanding officer of the platoon. That was in May 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in Sarajevo, do you know of any member of the Army of Republika Srpska on that front that was disciplined for breach of any offence?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I may --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that there was a court-martial in Zagrebacka Street.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Not court-martial. I meant military tribunal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A military tribunal. Did you hear of any soldier of the arm that you served in being disciplined at that place?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that if you had a reliable 120 millimetre round you could hit a target within 50 metres. If you had pre-existing coordinates for that target, would you be able to hit it first shot?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I would like things to be precise by saying exactly where the witness said this. Also I just want to say that considering we are very interested in the tapes and the transcript, I will need a couple of minutes at the end of the session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am afraid, Mr. President, that I am prepared to proceed now, but it seems if I will not be able to complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It looks as if we could not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But perhaps I could proceed on to the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I just answer the previous question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, the previous question has was an objection against that question. Mr. Piletta-Zanin --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Page 89 line 1 on the English transcript if I could -- page 81, line 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's where we find the 50 metres. Perhaps the Chamber should consider how to proceed because I take it that you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, will not be able to re-examine the witness, if there is any need to do so. I take it that there is need. Mr. Stamp, that would mean that we cannot conclude today, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I before you proceed, Mr. President, just ask for the answer to the last question before we move on to anything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The last question was -- let me just -- yes. Perhaps -- the last question, Mr. Stamp --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It is on page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please repeat that question and ask the witness to answer it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you had pre-existing coordinates for a target and you had fired into the area or the vicinity of that target before, would you thereafter be able to hit that target within 50 metres first shot?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC
utterances.text: Only in ideal conditions. And there you have to take into consideration other factors. Humidity, outside temperature, temperature of the air, temperature of the weapons which is rarely taken into consideration. Now, all these and I don't know if they exist. But this hit would be for a short [as interpreted] hit. I am saying that within 50 metre range, 50 [Realtime transcript read in error "15"] metre radius, you could hit. With some further shots you would be able to hit the target, with corrections. The temperature, humidity and all the other factors, even air pressure and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You explained that. Yes. I take it that -- did you say now 50 metres away because in the transcript, as you see for the second time it appears 15. But did you intend to change or did you still--

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are the regulations of the former JNA. I have to clarify. We used --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am just asking --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I am asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think since we are referring to the transcript, for that paragraph, I think he said "for a first hit" and not "for a short hit."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
