utterances.text: Yes. That's also what I -- and that's logical as well in respect of the what follows in his answer. We will not be able to conclude your testimony today, unfortunately because there are still more questions to be put to you by, I take it by the Prosecution. How much time would you still need, approximately, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I propose to try to complete within 30 minutes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you are asking for another 30 minutes. Are you still available for next Monday because it is the weekend that comes now? Would you be available next Monday, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are nodding and I take it that you are confirming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. But I understood that the examination will continue now, today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We tried to finish, but we have to leave this courtroom unless we can do a similar thing as we did yesterday, but I don't know whether that is possible. Is there already any schedule you to leave The Hague, has there been any plans?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There would be no plans. Could perhaps -- I think the Chamber first wants to consider whether it is of any use to try to continue this afternoon. May I first ask whether the parties could continue this afternoon? If necessary, I am not saying we are going to try, but I am just asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you very much. It has functioned very well yesterday thanks to the Chamber. But today I am expected in Geneva for a meeting and I have a plane at 4.00 and I don't really see how I can do it otherwise, except to be at this meeting tonight. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, would you be available?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have a meeting from 15.30 in the Detention Unit. It is an interview. And for a week I haven't had a conversation with the General, and bearing in mind his health, I don't know how he feels today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Efforts as we made yesterday should be an exception rather than a rule, therefore the Chamber decides that we will continue next Monday with your testimony. Witness is available, parties might have problems this afternoon. So we will adjourn until next Monday but then in the afternoon. If there would be anything the parties would like to address the Chamber at this very moment, we can see whether we can do that in five minutes, but let's first ask the usher to escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I -- before doing so. Witness, may I -- no, please. You are not allowed to speak with anyone, no one, about your testimony in this court. We will continue next Tuesday, so that's valid for -- next Monday -- yes, I said Tuesday, but it is Monday. So don't speak with anyone not with the Prosecution, not with the Defence, not with anyone about your testimony of today. Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, you were at your feet and Mr. Piletta-Zanin is on his feet as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. I had indicated earlier that I would be asking in order to prepare better for next week, if we could have directions in respect to the Rule -- I can't quote it now, but the facts that must be summarised upon instead of these generic facts. They are too general for any type of preparation. Where there is a wrong, there is a remedy, the remedy could not be, I think, to stop the witness from testifying. The only thing that I would ask is that the Defence be told that they need to be more precise and to be given guidance in that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will consider this matter and if this would result in whatever guidance then I take it that your addresses are known. If this guidance needs to be given today, we have to consider that, the Judges will have to discuss the matter. I take it that a message could reach you if necessary. Is there any other issue? Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, very briefly. I want to say again what I have already said privately to the representatives of the Defence which didn't go across very well. But all the indications that we had in the letter dated 29th of October for general purposes, would mutatis mutandis, would be valid for all the military people. This is a scheme that we wanted to impose for everyone line by line, situation by situation, weapon by weapon. So we would have to take that, copy it and put the names. So I believe here this is clear. However, the second thing, and this is all I am going to say, Mr. President, bearing in mind the interpretations, I have to say, the translation I believe, I can never be certain, and perhaps my reaction earlier was very quick, because I thought I heard something in Serbian, I wasn't sure, but I believe that for another matter, this witness said that he saw two people maneuvering this mortar, 82 millimetre, that is on page 32 of the transcript. Now, that is for the Serbian into English. The second thing in page 88 with respect to the French transcript, this is the second platoon we are talking about, and again for the French transcript, to conclude, we are not talking about firing at a distance, that would be very dangerous. I believe we are talking about an area of 50 metres, 50 metre radius. So again we have to be precise here. Others are just details. Yesterday I didn't have time to do, to say anything, and I just wanted to do the same thing. I apologise, the expression "high risk" that the witness used cannot be translated into French as "higher responsibility." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for your observations, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I would like to thank everyone in and around the courtroom for the patience because I must apologise that we took 10 minutes extra of your time. Thank you very much. I wish a good weekend to everyone and we will adjourn until next Monday, 2.15 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1.55 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 4th day of November, 2002, at 2.15 p.m. 24 25 Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.
